text:
Renee: heads-up — found a parity bug in the SDK listRoutes pagination vs REST. SDK uses page/limit params and returns a flattened array, but the REST API uses a cursor ('next_cursor') and can reorder results during concurrent writes. sample-app onboarding relies on complete listing and is missing routes, creating duplicates later.

Sam: can you paste a repro? which sdk/lang/version?

Renee: repro (ts-sdk@3.2.1):
```ts
// SDK call
const all = []
let page = 1
while (true) {
  const res = await client.routes.list({ page, limit: 50 })
  all.push(...res.routes)
  if (!res.hasMore) break
  page++
}
// res.routes is ordered by server processing order, but server's cursor-based list can return new items between pages
```

Renee: curl REST returns cursor metadata: 
```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.redwood.example/v1/routes?limit=50&cursor=abc123" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# -> {"data":[...], "next_cursor":"def456"}
```

Renee: in staging we saw this sequence: page1 returned routes A..Y, page2 (page=2) returned Z..ZZ but server would have returned some new route NN between Y and Z if using cursor; SDK page logic lost NN. sample-app then tried to create NN later and got a conflict or duplicate depending on timing.

Jamie: oh nice catch. SDK should be using the API's cursor model not page numbers. any logs?

Renee: logs show "GET /v1/routes?page=2&limit=50 -> 200 [normalized]" and SDK drops cursor from raw response. server-side audit shows NN created after page1 was generated but before page2; cursor-based fetch would surface it.

Priya: workaround: sample-app will switch to REST cursor flow for listing until SDK fix. pushing patch sampleapp/fix-listing.

Sam: why did SDK adopt page/limit? was that historical?

Jamie: older internal APIs used page numbers; when we migrated to cursor-based list on the server, some SDKs kept a compatibility shim translating cursor->page semantics. looks like the shim assumes stable paging and breaks with concurrent writes. bad idea.

Renee: effect on onboarding: sometimes missing initial check causes sample-app to attempt create -> 409 conflict, which onboarding treats as fatal in a couple places. other times it creates duplicates in staging causing confusion.

Sam: proposed fix: 1) SDK should expose raw cursor fields (next_cursor) and a cursor-based iterator API; 2) keep convenience page/limit helpers but implement them by looping over cursors under the hood, preserving server ordering; 3) document concurrency caveat.

Jamie: I'll open RED-5700 and draft a PR to change TS/JS SDK behavior. PR will add a `.listAll({ limit, cursor })` async iterator that yields items in server order and preserves next_cursor in the response. We'll also add a flag `compat.usePageNumbers=true` to preserve old behavior temporarily.

Priya: add integration tests that simulate concurrent creates between pages and assert iterator returns the new items. Also update sample-app tests to use iterator.

Renee: putting a short-term guard in sample-app to detect 409 during create and reconcile by re-listing with cursor-based REST call. will revert once SDK patch ships.

devx-bot: Created issue RED-5700: "SDK pagination parity: adopt cursor-based iteration and expose next_cursor" assigned to @Jamie, priority P2.

Jamie: plan: ship patch in 3.2.2 with iterator and raw cursor exposure, add migration note in changelog, and schedule a canary on staging. ETA: 48h. anyone object?

Sam: no objections. please note for other SDKs (py/go) to keep parity.

Renee: thanks all — will monitor staging and revert the sample-app guard after canary :thumbsup:
